note.note:
History and Physical (H&P – Super Detailed)

Consult Summary:
60-year-old male with hypertension, 15-pack-year smoking history, and strong family history of premature myocardial infarction presents with 2-hour episode of central chest pressure radiating to the left arm, associated with diaphoresis, shortness of breath, and nausea; ambulance activated for suspected acute coronary syndrome.

History:
• Presenting complaint: Central “pressure” in chest “like someone sitting on my chest.”  
• Onset: Began suddenly while kneeling and gardening ~2 hours prior to video visit.  
• Course/progression: Persistent and unchanged at time of consult.  
• Location/Radiation: Diffuse mid-chest; radiates to left arm and shoulder.  
• Severity: Not numerically rated; described as uncomfortable pressure.  
• Associated symptoms: Nausea (no vomiting), diaphoresis, shortness of breath, subjective palpitations (likely stress-related).  
• Exacerbating/relieving factors: None identified; occurred during light activity, not relieved spontaneously.  
• Prior episodes: None.  
• Review of systems (limited):  
  – Cardiovascular: Chest pressure, left-arm radiation, palpitations. Denies previous similar pain.  
  – Respiratory: Shortness of breath; no cough reported.  
  – GI: Nausea; no vomiting, heartburn, or reflux symptoms reported.  
  – Constitutional: Diaphoresis.  
  – Neurologic, musculoskeletal, GU: Not discussed.

Past Medical History:
• Hypertension – duration not specified; current treatment not discussed.  
• No known diabetes.  
• Cholesterol status never checked.  
• No prior cardiac events reported.

Medications:
• None documented.

Allergies:
• Aspirin – mild swelling reaction (non-life-threatening).

Social History:
• Tobacco: Smokes ~10 cigarettes/day for 15 years.  
• Alcohol: ~7–8 pints of beer per week.  
• Illicit drugs: None reported.  
• Activity level: Generally low; minimal regular exercise.  
• Weight: Patient acknowledges being overweight (exact weight/BMI not provided).  
• Living situation: Lives alone; front door left open for EMS access.  
• Occupation: Restaurant owner (sushi shop).

Family History:
• Father: Died of myocardial infarction at ~60 years.  
• Mother: “Heart problems” (details unspecified).

Physical Examination:
(Conducted via video)  
• General: Appears uncomfortable, diaphoretic, and short of breath.  
• Vitals: Not available.  
• Cardiac, respiratory, abdominal, extremity exams: Unable to perform remotely.

Investigations:
• None completed yet. Plan for pre-hospital ECG on ambulance arrival.

Assessment & Plan:
Issue 1 – Acute central chest pain, highly suspicious for Acute Coronary Syndrome (ACS; possible myocardial infarction)
  • Rationale: Ongoing central pressure, left-arm radiation, diaphoresis, dyspnoea, nausea, multiple CAD risk factors, positive family history.  
  • Plan:  
    – Emergency medical services activated; clinician remained on line until arrival.  
    – Pre-hospital 12-lead ECG and cardiac monitoring.  
    – Hospital evaluation with serial ECGs, cardiac enzymes, chest X-ray.  
    – Oxygen and analgesia as needed.  
    – Antiplatelet therapy: Aspirin generally indicated but patient has mild allergy; relay allergy details to EMS/hospital to consider risk-benefit or alternative agents (e.g., clopidogrel).  
    – Nitroglycerin and morphine per ACS protocol if not contraindicated.  
    – Consider heparin/PCI per cardiology.

Issue 2 – Chronic hypertension
  • Rationale: Self-reported history; uncontrolled status unknown.  
  • Plan (deferred until after acute event):  
    – Review current antihypertensive regimen and blood-pressure logs.  
    – Initiate/adjust therapy per guidelines post-ACS work-up.  
    – Monitor renal function and electrolytes.

Issue 3 – Modifiable cardiovascular risk factors
  • Smoking cessation: Provide counselling, consider nicotine replacement or pharmacotherapy post-hospitalisation.  
  • Weight management and physical activity counselling post-event.  
  • Alcohol intake within moderate range; reassess later.  
  • Lipid profile: Order fasting lipid panel once stable; consider statin.

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx):
1. Acute coronary syndrome (MI/unstable angina) – High likelihood: Classic symptom cluster, multiple risk factors, positive family history.  
2. Aortic dissection – Moderate likelihood: Sudden chest pain in hypertensive smoker; less typical “pressure” quality and no back pain noted, but must be excluded in ED.  
3. Pulmonary embolism – Low–Moderate likelihood: Acute dyspnoea and chest discomfort; lacks pleuritic nature or major risk factors.

Quality checks:
● Missing/expected elements: Current medication list, complete allergies (only aspirin documented), vital signs, full review of systems, baseline BP readings, past surgical history.  
● Conflicts: None identified between transcript and DDx.  
● Transcript quality: Clear audio; no significant gaps, but limited physical exam and ROS due to telehealth context.
